title: Suicide Deaths Among People Aged 15 to 24 Are 1.9 Times as Many as Cancer Deaths: A Global Census of Registered Deaths and a Systematic Review
content: Background: Suicide is often said to kill more young people than cancer, but the size of the difference has rarely been quantified. Methods: we analysed registered deaths at ages 15 to 24 from the WHO Mortality Database, Eurostat for the European Union, and WHO Global Health Estimates as a modelled comparison, and conducted a PRISMA 2020 systematic review of MEDLINE via PubMed and Europe PMC, supplemented by OpenAlex and Crossref, to establish whether the quantity had already been reported. Ages 15 to 24 were used because no multi-country source publishes the 18 to 25 band. Results: in the 66 countries with low ill-defined-cause coding, 24,040 suicide deaths and 12,778 cancer deaths gave a ratio of 1.88 (95% CI 1.84 to 1.92); the ratio was 3.07 in high-income countries and 2.25 in males against 1.32 in females. On a balanced panel of 56 countries it widened by 43 per cent between 2005 and 2022, because registered cancer deaths fell while suicide deaths rose. Of 696 screened records plus a supplementary search, 23 studies were eligible and none of the 12 reports obtained states the ratio. Conclusions: where cause of death is relatively well coded, suicide accounts for close to twice as many deaths at ages 15 to 24 as cancer, and for about three times as many in high-income countries.
